title: The visual fields of the frog and toad: a comparative study
why: It would set the frog's and toad's field of view and binocular overlap, which the frog view now guesses.

title: A linear area centralis extending across the turtle retina and stabilized to the horizon by non-visual cues
why: It would show whether the turtle's sharp band should stay level with the horizon as the phone tilts.

title: The imaging properties and sensitivity of the facial pits of pitvipers as determined by optical and heat-transfer analysis
why: It would give the pit organ's field of view and optical blur, which set the size and softness of the heat glow.

title: An ecological correlate of critical flicker-fusion frequencies for some Anolis lizards
why: It would give anole flicker fusion, which sets the anole view's pace and is the nearest value for other lizards.

title: The aerial and aquatic visual acuity of the optomotor response in the crested newt (Triturus cristatus)
why: It would give a newt's acuity by behaviour in air and in water, which sets the salamander view's sharpness.

title: Gecko vision: retinal organization, foveae and implications for binocular vision
why: It would give gecko foveae and acuity, which the gecko view now borrows from anoles.

title: Retinal ganglion cell topography and visual acuity of the sleepy lizard (Tiliqua rugosa)
why: It would give a skink's acuity and retinal topography for the lizard view's sharpness and sharp spot.

title: Animal Eyes, 2nd edition, chapters 4 to 9 (pp. 72 to 242)
why: The owner's copy came through only to about p. 66, and chapter 5 (Lens eyes on land, with Amphibious eyes at p. 117) and chapter 9 (Movements of the eyes) would check the optics, pupils and eye movements behind every view here.

authors: Heath JE, Northcutt RG, Barber RP
title: Rotational optokinesis in reptiles and its bearing on pupillary shape
why: It would check the slit and round pupils in the alligator, gecko, pitviper and lizard views against measured eye movements.

title: Ophthalmology of Crocodilia: alligators, crocodiles, caimans, and gharials
why: It would check the crocodilian pupil, tapetum and field-of-view rows against a veterinary review.

title: Wavelength discrimination in the turtle Pseudemys scripta elegans
why: It would confirm by behaviour the four-cone colour vision that the turtle view's colour rows rest on.

title: The visual acuity of the frog (Rana pipiens)
why: It would give the full method and conditions behind the frog view's 2.8 cycles per degree, now taken from a conference abstract.

title: Motion detection in the presence and absence of background motion in an Anolis lizard
why: It would set how strongly the anole view damps movement when the whole scene sways.

title: Infrared imaging in vipers: differential responses of crotaline and viperine snakes to paired thermal targets
why: It would show whether true vipers without pits respond to heat, which decides whether they belong in the heat view.

authors: Grace MS, Woodward OM, Church DR, Calisch G
title: Prey targeting by the infrared-imaging snake Python molurus: effects of experimental and congenital visual deprivation
why: It would confirm that pythons can aim strikes by heat alone, which places pythons and boas in the heat view.

authors: Gracheva EO, Ingolia NT, Kelly YM, Cordero-Morales JF, Hollopeter G, Chesler AT, Sanchez EE, Pérez JC, Weissman JS, Julius DJ
title: Molecular basis of infrared detection by snakes
why: It is the primary source for the heat-sensing channel of pit vipers, boas and pythons, open in PubMed Central, though every route to it returned a rate limit or a bot check.

title: Thermoregulatory function of the parietal eye in the lizard Anolis carolinensis
why: It would show how the parietal eye changes basking in anoles, which bears on the third-eye strip.

authors: Bartol S, Musick JA, Ochs AL
title: Visual acuity thresholds of juvenile loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta): an electrophysiological approach
why: It would give a sea turtle's acuity for comparison with the pond slider's.

title: The role of visual and olfactory cues in the prey catching behavior of the tiger salamander, Ambystoma tigrinum
why: It would weigh sight against smell in a salamander's strike, which sets the strength of the salamander view's movement gate.

title: Prey detection by vomeronasal chemoreception in a plethodontid salamander
why: It would support the salamander view's smell row with a measured vomeronasal response to prey.
